title: Marketplace assimilation slate and copy checklist
content:
Purpose

This is a working slate to align on copy variants, acceptance gates, and the technical preflight for partner listings across multiple cloud marketplaces. Goal: produce a single-asset bundle that can be ingested by AWS/GCP/Azure publishing flows without repeatedly reworking basic metadata. Treat as source-of-truth for the current partner sprint (v0.3).

Quick context notes (notes-to-self):
- Use concise value propositions that emphasize: predictable inference, cost controls, private deployments (VPC/on-prem), and SLA-backed Dedicated capacity.
- Target audience splits: ISV integrators, platform engineering buyers, and procurement/security reviewers.
- Keep micro-copy separate from long-form benefits to enable A/B on tile vs detail page.

Copy variants (do not finalize without legal review):
1) Tile-level headline (<= 30 chars):
- "Predictable LLM inference"
- "High-throughput LLM runtime"

2) Short description (80-110 chars):
- "Run LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with cost and latency guards."
- "Fast, reliable LLM serving with versioned rollouts, autoscaling GPUs, and tenant isolation."

3) 250–400 char detail blurb (marketing page):
- "Redwood Inference delivers production-grade LLM inference across hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem deployments. Ship features with predictable latency, transparent token economics, and first-class rollout + observability tooling—so engineering teams can focus on product not infrastructure."

4) Enterprise-focused paragraph (for legal/SSO/SLA readers):
- "Enterprise teams can provision Dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed latency targets, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and optional private control planes. Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts, automatic fallback policies, and multi-region routing for resilience and compliance."

Suggested feature bullets (UI-friendly):
- Hosted API: REST/SDKs, streaming, function calling
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, autoscale, burst capacity
- Private: VPC/on-prem control plane, KMS/HSM support
- Optimize: batching/caching recommendations, quantization tips
- Console: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards

Listing metadata fields (draft values to copy into marketplace consoles):
- Short name: Redwood Inference (Hosted + Dedicated + Private)
- Category: AI / Developer Tools / ML Ops
- Supported regions: North America, Europe, APAC (partners)
- Pricing model: usage-based + reserved capacity options
- Trial: 14-day trial credits (auto-provisioned)

Technical preflight checklist (must be green before vendor submission):
- [ ] SKU mapping confirmed (console SKU to Redwood billing SKU)
- [ ] Trial entitlement flow: how credits are granted and revoked (diagram + test account)
- [ ] Billing contract type clarified (marketplace-billable vs self-bill)
- [ ] Metering event sample payloads attached (token counts, embedding calls, inference_duration_ms)
- [ ] SSO/OAuth: OIDC config documented + test tenant available (okta/google)
- [ ] Security: SOC2 scope note, encryption-at-rest, KMS integration doc attached
- [ ] Data handling: customer data residency notes and retention policy in plain text
- [ ] Private deployment compatibility: IP allowlist & network topologies (VPC peering, on-prem options)
- [ ] Support SLA and escalation path included (email + PagerDuty play)
- [ ] Legal: TOS/Privacy pointers and marketplace-specific amendments flagged
- [ ] Artifacts: screenshots (console, dashboards), architecture diagram (svg/pdf), logo assets (SVG/PNG)

Acceptance test scenarios (quick smoke list):
- Provision trial account via marketplace -> confirm trial credits appear in console within 10 minutes.
- Execute 1k tokens generation via hosted API using marketplace-provisioned keys -> validate token-metering record in sample billing export.
- Create Dedicated pool via marketplace flow (reserved commitment) -> verify pool in provisioning API and run simple latency test.
- Simulate SSO login (OIDC) with partner tenant -> confirm user is created and role mapping applied.

Launch runbook snippets (for partner engineer + ops):
- 0–30 min: Validate marketplace listing renders (tile + short description).
- 30–90 min: Create a marketplace trial account, capture api-keys, run smoke generation and embedding calls.
- 90–240 min: Run billing export, reconcile charges to test events, validate SKU mapping.
- Post-launch 0–72 hrs: Monitor telemetries for token anomalies, error spikes, and onboarding friction (views -> signups -> trial->paid).

Edge cases & failure modes to call out to partner PMs: 
- Marketplace truncates long descriptions: provide short variant as fallback.
- Image assets get resized; provide 3 sizes and confirm aspect ratio.
- Some marketplaces force separate legal amendments for BYOL/private deployments—pre-clear with legal.

Open questions (needs input before final submission):
- Can we standardize the trial credit amount across AWS/GCP/Azure or must it be negotiated per-store? (@Miguel Torres)
- Do we expose a marketplace-specific promo code logic or route everything through Redwood billing? (@Rae Patel)
- Who owns the marketplace support SLAs at night (redwood on-call vs partner)? Need an explicit escalation matrix.

Slack & ticket refs (working links):
- Slack: #go-to-market-marketplace (thread: convo 11/2025, "tile sizing issue")
- Jira: JIRA-7342 (marketplace SKU mapping), JIRA-7499 (trial flow bug)

Next steps / owners (short):
- Copy freeze for QA: submit candidate copy to legal review by 2025-11-15. Owner: Ava Chen.
- Technical preflight: engineering to produce meter examples + test tenant by 2025-11-10. Owner: Jonah Li.
- Billing & SKU: finance to provide SKU mapping doc and charges preview by 2025-11-12. Owner: Miguel Torres.

Notes to reviewer (informal):
- This is intentionally terse — the aim is to cut back-and-forth during console entry. Keep one canonical short-headline and one canonical 250-char blurb; everything else can be derived.
- If we end up shipping marketplace-specific variants, track them here (append date + marketplace tag).

End of slate.
